incoming.name: Earth
incoming.excerpt: During the Devonian period, there were 400 days in a year, with each day lasting 21.8 hours.

incoming.name: Plant
incoming.excerpt: Vascular plants first appeared during the Silurian period, and by the Devonian had diversified and spread into many different land environments.

outgoing.name: Australia
outgoing.excerpt: A great barrier reef, now left high and dry in the Kimberley Basin of northwest Australia, once extended a thousand kilometers, fringing a Devonian continent.

outgoing.name: Carbon dioxide
outgoing.excerpt: The 'greening' of the continents acted as a carbon dioxide sink, and atmospheric levels of this greenhouse gas may have dropped.

outgoing.name: Evolution
outgoing.excerpt: While fish underwent a major radiation it was only one of several major evolutionary landmarks during the period, and other lifeforms were more common.

outgoing.name: Fern
outgoing.excerpt: By the Late Devonian, forests of small, primitive plants existed: lycophytes, sphenophytes, ferns, and progymnosperms had evolved.

outgoing.name: Planet
outgoing.excerpt: The deep, enormous Panthalassa (the "universal ocean") covered the rest of the planet.

outgoing.name: Shark
outgoing.excerpt: In the oceans, fish diversified into the first sharks, and the first lobe-finned and bony fish.

outgoing.name: Vertebrate
outgoing.excerpt: Also in the Devonian, both vertebrates and arthropods were solidly established on the land.

outgoing.name: Wood
outgoing.excerpt: The tree-like ancestral fern Archaeopteris, grew as a large tree with true wood.
